how-to-make-a-round-robin-schedule.html.text:
← League schedule generator

How to make a round-robin schedule, with a worked example

A round robin is the simplest fair league: every team plays every other team the same number of times. The hard part is not the pairing, it is everything around it: the odd team who sits out each week, who is at home, which court, and the team captain who cannot play on the 20th.

Open the free schedule generator

A worked example

Five invented pickleball teams play on Tuesday evenings from 6 October 2026 on two courts. Five teams means five rounds of two matches, and each team has one bye. The home team is listed first.

RoundDateCourt 1Court 2Bye
16 OctBolts v EaglesDinks v CometsAces
213 OctComets v AcesEagles v DinksBolts
320 OctDinks v BoltsAces v EaglesComets
427 OctEagles v CometsBolts v AcesDinks
53 NovAces v DinksComets v BoltsEagles

Every pair meets once (ten matches), every team hosts twice and visits twice, nobody has two home or two away games in a row, and each team plays twice on each court. The generator checks all of that with a separate validator before it shows you the result. Bring a blackout date, for example Comets away on 20 October, and only the one match that clashes moves, to a makeup round on the next free Tuesday.

Make your own schedule

Questions

What is a round-robin schedule?

A format where every team plays every other team the same number of times. A single round robin with n teams has n(n-1)/2 matches; a double round robin plays each pair twice, once at each team's home venue. It is the fairest way to rank a small league because nobody is knocked out and the table is decided by everyone's results against everyone.

What happens with an odd number of teams?

The circle method adds an invisible extra team, so each round one real team has a bye. Five teams play five rounds and every team sits out exactly once. The generator lists the bye in each round so the team knows it is not playing that week.

How do you keep home and away fair?

In the circle method the home side of each pairing is set while the rounds are built, not patched afterwards. With an even number of teams the minimum possible number of home or away breaks (two consecutive home games or two consecutive away games) is the number of teams minus two, and the generator reaches it. With an odd number of teams no team gets two home or two away games in a row. A double round robin is mirrored, so every pair plays once at each home.

What if a team cannot play on a certain date?

Type the team and the date as a blackout. The generator moves only the affected match out of that round and plays it in a makeup round after the regular season, so the other teams are not held up. If a date has to be given up entirely, it says so. Check the makeup dates with the teams before you publish.

No warranty. Free and as-is, without warranty of any kind. This page is general information, not legal or financial advice. Check every date, court and pairing before you send a schedule to a league. The example teams are invented.

Everything the generator does runs in your browser; team names and dates are never uploaded. Free and open source: support is entirely optional.

how-to-run-a-double-elimination-tourname.text:
← League schedule generator

How to run a double-elimination tournament: winners bracket, losers bracket and the reset

In double elimination a team is out only after its second loss. That makes it fairer than single elimination for tournaments where teams travelled and one bad game should not end the weekend. The price is roughly twice the games.

Open the free bracket builder (set the play-off to double elimination on the page)

A worked example: 6 teams, 10 games

Six invented teams are seeded 1 to 6. The bracket is sized to 8, so the #1 and #2 seeds get a first-round bye. Teams that lose in the winners bracket drop into the losers bracket; a second loss ends their run. Matches are named so you can follow who plays whom: "winner of W2M1" is whoever wins that game.

RoundMatchTeams
Winners QuarterfinalsW1M2#4 Bears vs #5 Lynx
Winners QuarterfinalsW1M4#3 Foxes vs #6 Wolves
Winners SemifinalsW2M1#1 Hawks vs winner of W1M2
Winners SemifinalsW2M2#2 Owls vs winner of W1M4
Winners FinalW3M1winner of W2M1 vs winner of W2M2
Losers round 2 (WB drop-downs)L2M1loser of W1M2 vs loser of W2M2
Losers round 2 (WB drop-downs)L2M2loser of W1M4 vs loser of W2M1
Losers round 3L3M1winner of L2M1 vs winner of L2M2
Losers round 4 (WB drop-downs)L4M1winner of L3M1 vs loser of W3M1
Grand finalGF1winner of W3M1 vs winner of L4M1
Grand final reset (only if the losers-bracket team wins GF1)GF2winner of GF1 vs loser of GF1

If the losers-bracket team wins GF1, a reset game GF2 is played between the same two teams, which makes 11 games. Otherwise the tournament ends after GF1.

The bracket comes from the same code the page runs and a test recomputes this table from it, so it cannot drift from the tool.

Build your own bracket

Questions

How many games is a double-elimination tournament?

With 6 teams it is 10 games, or 11 if the grand final reset is needed. In general a double-elimination field of n teams plays between 2n - 2 and 2n - 1 games, because every team except the champion loses exactly twice and the reset game is played only when the losers-bracket team wins the grand final.

What is a grand final reset?

The winners-bracket finalist has not lost yet, the losers-bracket finalist has lost once. If the losers-bracket team wins the grand final, both teams now have one loss, so a second game decides the title. If the winners-bracket team wins the first game, the tournament is over.

How do byes work when the field is not a power of two?

The bracket is sized up to the next power of two (8 for 6 teams) and the top seeds skip the first round. In the example, the #1 and #2 seeds have a first-round bye, and the losers bracket skips every match a bye leaves without an opponent.

When should I use double elimination instead of single?

Use it when one bad game should not end a team's weekend, such as a youth or rec tournament where every team travelled. It costs about twice the games of a single-elimination bracket, so check you have the courts and daylight for them.

how-to-run-a-mexicano-tournament.html.text:
← League schedule generator

How to run a Mexicano: draw each round from the standings

A Mexicano is a social doubles format for padel, pickleball, badminton and tennis nights. Round one is a random draw. After that, every round is drawn from the table, so players with similar scores end up on the same court and the night gets closer as it goes. Like an Americano, nobody needs a fixed partner and your own points count towards your own total.

Open the free Mexicano draw (the Mexicano card on the page: enter players, courts and finished games)

A worked example: 8 players, 2 courts

Eight invented players on two courts. Round one is a seeded random draw:

RoundCourtSide ASide B
11Ben & GusCy & Fay
12Ana & DeeEli & Hal

The scores come back as Ben & Gus 21-14 Cy & Fay and Ana & Dee 17-21 Eli & Hal. Each player is credited with their side's points:

RankPlayerPointsDiff
1Ben21+7
2Gus21+7
3Eli21+4
4Hal21+4
5Ana17-4
6Dee17-4
7Cy14-7
8Fay14-7

Ranked 1 to 8, the table is cut into groups of four. In each group the top player partners the bottom player against the middle two (1 & 4 against 2 & 3). Round two:

RoundCourtSide ASide B
21Ben & HalEli & Gus
22Ana & FayCy & Dee

Court 1 has the leaders, court 2 the chasers, and nobody repeats a partner. The draw is deterministic for a given seed, and a separate test recomputes this example from the same code the tool runs.

Draw your own round

Questions

How is a Mexicano different from an Americano?

An Americano fixes every pairing in advance so everyone partners as many different people as possible. A Mexicano draws each round after the first from the standings, so players with similar scores meet and the night tightens up as it goes. The tool has both: Build rotation for Americano and Draw next round for Mexicano.

How do you pair a Mexicano round?

Rank the players by points so far and cut the list into groups of four. In each group the top player partners the bottom player against the second and third: 1 & 4 against 2 & 3. If that would repeat a partnership, the tool picks a split that repeats fewer.

Who sits out when the number of players is not a multiple of 4?

Each court needs 4 players, so the extras sit out. The tool sits out whoever has played the most games so far, with a random tie-break, so games stay within one of even.

How do you score a Mexicano?

Each player is credited with the points their side scored in every game, so a strong partner never costs you. Players are ranked by points for, then points difference, then wins. This tool draws the rounds and keeps the table; it is not a rating system.

Related: how an Americano rotation works, how to make a round-robin schedule for team leagues, and how a Swiss tournament works.

← League schedule generator

How to seed and run a single-elimination bracket, with a worked example

Single elimination is the quickest way to find one winner: lose once and you are out. It suits play-offs at the end of a league, one-day pickleball, darts or esports events, and any tournament where courts or daylight are short. The two decisions that go wrong by hand are the seeding order and the byes when the number of teams is not 4, 8 or 16.

Open the free bracket tool (type the teams best seed first; dates continue from your league on the weekdays you choose)

A worked example: 6 teams, 5 games

Six invented teams are seeded 1 to 6. The bracket is sized up to 8 slots, and the two empty slots become byes for the top two seeds, so the #1 and #2 seeds skip the first round. Seeds 1 and 2 are on opposite halves, so they can only meet in the final. "Winner of R1M2" is whoever wins that game.

RoundMatchTeams
QuarterfinalsR1M2#4 Bears vs #5 Lynx
QuarterfinalsR1M4#3 Foxes vs #6 Wolves
SemifinalsR2M1#1 Hawks vs winner of R1M2
SemifinalsR2M2#2 Owls vs winner of R1M4
FinalR3M1winner of R2M1 vs winner of R2M2

The #1 and #2 seeds play only two games to win the title; the other four teams play three. That is the reward for a good league finish, and why seeding should come from standings rather than from who signed up first.

The bracket comes from the same code the page runs and a test recomputes this table from it, so it cannot drift from the tool.

Build your own bracket

Questions

How many games are in a single-elimination tournament?

Always one fewer than the number of teams, whatever the size, because every team except the champion loses exactly once. Six teams play 5 games; sixteen teams play 15.

How does seeding work in a single-elimination bracket?

The bracket is filled so that seed 1 meets the lowest seed, seed 2 the second lowest, and so on, and so that the top seeds can only meet each other late: seeds 1 and 2 are on opposite halves and cannot meet before the final. In an 8-slot bracket the first-round pairings are 1 v 8, 4 v 5, 2 v 7 and 3 v 6.

How do byes work when the number of teams is not a power of two?

The bracket is sized up to the next power of two (8 for 6 teams, 16 for 12) and the empty slots go to the lowest seeds, so the top seeds skip round one. With 6 teams the #1 and #2 seeds have a bye; with 12 teams the top four do.

How many rounds does a single-elimination bracket have?

The base-2 logarithm of the bracket size, rounded up: 3 rounds for 5 to 8 teams, 4 rounds for 9 to 16 teams. A bye does not remove a round; the team just plays its first game in round two.

When is single elimination the wrong choice?

When every team has travelled and expects more than one game, or when seeding is a guess. A round robin or a double-elimination bracket gives each team more games, at the cost of more courts and time.

how-to-run-a-swiss-tournament.html.text:
← League schedule generator

How to run a Swiss-system tournament, with a worked example

A Swiss tournament is for a club night or a weekend event with more players than there is time for a round robin. Nobody is knocked out, everyone plays every round, and each round pairs people who are doing about equally well. Chess clubs, darts leagues, board-game and card-game events use it.

Open the free pairing tool (it is the Swiss card on the page; pair each round by pasting in the results so far)

A worked example

Six invented players, seeded in the order they signed up. Six players need 3 rounds. Round 1 has no scores yet, so the seed order decides: the top half plays the bottom half.

Round 1WhiteBlack
Board 1AnaDee
Board 2BenEli
Board 3CyFay

Suppose Ana, Ben and Fay win. The three winners now have 1 point and the three losers 0, so round 2 pairs winners with winners and losers with losers, with nobody meeting a previous opponent:

Round 2WhiteBlack
Board 1AnaBen
Board 2FayDee
Board 3EliCy

Fay, on 1 point, plays Dee, on 0, because the other two 1-point players already meet each other: the tool shows that as a "floater" and says so rather than hiding it. Colours alternate, so nobody is white three times running. The pairing is checked by a separate validator before it is shown.

Pair your own round

Questions

How many rounds does a Swiss tournament need?

Enough that one player can be clearly ahead: the next whole number above log base 2 of the player count. Six or eight players need 3 rounds, sixteen need 4. More rounds sort the middle of the table more finely, but the top places are usually settled by this number.

How are players paired in a Swiss round?

Everyone is sorted by score, then players with the same score are paired top half against bottom half, so the strongest of a group meets the weakest of that group. Nobody plays the same opponent twice. In round 1 nobody has a score yet, so the seed order decides.

What happens with an odd number of players?

One player gets a bye each round and is scored as a win. The bye goes to the lowest-ranked player who has not had one yet, so nobody gets two byes before everyone has had one.

How are ties in the standings broken?

By Buchholz: the sum of your opponents' scores. Beating players who went on to do well is worth more than beating players who lost everything. Players still level after that keep their seed order.

Related: how to make a round-robin schedule for small leagues where everyone can play everyone.

how-to-run-an-americano-tournament.html.text:
← League schedule generator

How to run an Americano: rotating partners for padel, pickleball and badminton nights

An Americano is a social doubles format where everyone plays with and against as many different people as possible. Nobody needs a fixed partner, so it suits club nights, open mornings and mixed-level groups. Each round you get a new partner, and your own points count towards your own total.

Open the free rotation builder (the Americano card on the page: enter players, courts and rounds)

A worked example: 8 players, 2 courts, 7 rounds

Eight invented players on two courts play 7 rounds. Everyone plays every round, so there are no sit-outs. Every player partners each of the other seven players exactly once, and nobody plays the same partner twice.

RoundCourtSide ASide B
11Eli & FayBen & Gus
12Cy & HalAna & Dee
21Dee & HalFay & Gus
22Ben & EliAna & Cy
31Dee & GusAna & Ben
32Fay & HalCy & Eli
41Ben & FayAna & Hal
42Eli & GusCy & Dee
51Cy & FayAna & Gus
52Ben & DeeEli & Hal
61Gus & HalAna & Eli
62Ben & CyDee & Fay
71Ana & FayDee & Eli
72Cy & GusBen & Hal

The plan is built by a seeded search and then checked by a separate validator: nobody is on two courts in a round, and the counts of games and sit-outs are within one of even. The same seed gives the same plan, so you can rebuild it on another device.

Build your own rotation

Questions

How many rounds does an Americano have?

With 8 players and 2 courts, 7 rounds lets every player partner every other player exactly once. In general, with n players the full cycle is n - 1 rounds when n is a multiple of 4; shorter nights simply stop earlier, and the tool lets you pick any number of rounds.

What if the number of players is not a multiple of 4?

Each court needs 4 players, so the extras sit out. The tool shares sit-outs so nobody sits out more than one round more than anyone else, and it shares games the same way.

How do you score an Americano?

Each player keeps the points their side scored in every game, and the night's winner is the player with the most points. Games are usually played to a fixed score such as 21 or 24, or for a fixed time. This tool builds the rotation; it does not keep score or rate anyone.

What is the difference between Americano and Mexicano?

In an Americano the pairings are fixed in advance so everyone partners as many different people as possible. In a Mexicano, each round after the first is drawn from the standings, so players of similar level meet. The tool has both: Build rotation for Americano and Draw next round for Mexicano.

Related: how to make a round-robin schedule for team leagues, and how a Swiss tournament works.

how-to-schedule-a-league-with-limited-co.text:
← League schedule generator

How to schedule a league with limited courts and time slots, with a worked example

A round robin tells you who plays whom each week. It does not tell you which court or what time, and that is where hand-made schedules go wrong: a court booked twice, or one team stuck with the 8 pm slot all season. The rule is simple. Each round has half as many matches as teams (rounded down), and every match needs its own court-and-time slot.

Open the free schedule tool (list your courts and start times; slots are shared out for you)

A worked example: 6 teams, 2 courts, 2 start times

Six invented teams play a single round robin on Tuesdays: 5 rounds of 3 matches. Two courts at 18:00 and 19:00 give four slots a round, one more than needed. Home team is listed first.

RoundMatches (court and time)
1Bears v Foxes (Court A 18:00), Hawks v Wolves (Court A 19:00), Owls v Lynx (Court B 19:00)
2Wolves v Owls (Court A 18:00), Foxes v Hawks (Court B 18:00), Lynx v Bears (Court A 19:00)
3Hawks v Lynx (Court A 18:00), Bears v Owls (Court B 18:00), Foxes v Wolves (Court B 19:00)
4Owls v Hawks (Court A 18:00), Wolves v Bears (Court B 18:00), Lynx v Foxes (Court B 19:00)
5Lynx v Wolves (Court B 18:00), Foxes v Owls (Court A 19:00), Hawks v Bears (Court B 19:00)

Across the five rounds every team plays the 18:00 slot two or three times and the 19:00 slot two or three times, and no court is used twice at the same time. The assignment is a seeded search, so the same input always gives the same table.

The table comes from the same code the page runs and a test recomputes it, so it cannot drift from the tool.

Build your own schedule

Questions

How many courts do I need for a round robin?

Half the number of teams, rounded down, matches per round, so you need that many court-and-time slots in each round. Six teams play 3 matches a round: three courts at one time, or two courts at two times, or one court at three times. Count courts times time slots, not courts alone.

What happens if I do not have enough courts or time slots?

The tool refuses to build the schedule and says how many matches a round needs and how many your courts and times fit, rather than quietly double-booking a court. Add a court, add a time slot, or play fewer teams per night by splitting into pools.

How do I make early and late slots fair?

Count how many early slots each team gets across the season and keep the counts within one of each other. The tool assigns slots by seeded simulated annealing against that cost, so in the six-team example every team plays the 18:00 slot two or three times out of five.

Can a team that can only play early be given early slots?

Yes. Give that team a time limit such as Lob Squad: 17:00 and it is only offered slots that start by then; rainout moves respect the limit and the validator flags any breach.

Why does the same input always give the same schedule?

The slot search is seeded, so the same teams, courts, times and seed give the same schedule every time. Change the seed to get a different, equally valid arrangement.

how-to-schedule-a-round-robin-with-an-od.text:
← League schedule generator

How to schedule a round robin with an odd number of teams, with a worked example

With 6 or 8 teams everyone plays every round. With 5, 7 or 9 someone has to sit out each round, and doing that by hand usually ends with one team idle twice while another never rests. The fix is the circle method: add an imaginary extra team, schedule as if it were real, and whoever is paired with it has the bye.

Open the free schedule tool (paste the teams, pick a start date and weekday; byes are marked for you)

A worked example: 5 teams, 5 rounds, 10 games

Five invented teams play a single round robin. Each round has two games and one team on a bye, and every team has its bye in a different round. Home team is listed first.

RoundGamesBye
1Owls v Lynx, Bears v FoxesHawks
2Foxes v Hawks, Lynx v BearsOwls
3Bears v Owls, Hawks v LynxFoxes
4Lynx v Foxes, Owls v HawksBears
5Hawks v Bears, Foxes v OwlsLynx

Each team plays 4 games and rests once. If a team must be off in a particular week (a holiday, a venue clash), decide which team takes which line of the list before dates are attached, rather than moving single games afterwards.

The rounds come from the same code the page runs and a test recomputes this table from it, so it cannot drift from the tool.

Build your own schedule

Questions

How many rounds does a round robin with an odd number of teams have?

As many as there are teams: 5 teams need 5 rounds, 7 teams need 7. An even number of teams needs one fewer round than teams, because nobody sits out; an odd number adds a dummy team, and whoever is paired with it has the bye.

How many byes does each team get?

Exactly one in a single round robin, whatever the size. With 5 teams that is one idle round each across 5 rounds, with two games played in every round.

How many games are played in total?

n × (n − 1) ÷ 2, odd or even. Five teams play 10 games and seven teams play 21, because each team plays every other team once: 4 games each for 5 teams.

Is a bye fair when teams play on different dates?

Only if the bye falls in a different round for each team, which the circle method guarantees. If a team needs a particular week off, give them the round where they have the bye by choosing which team takes which line of the list before dates are set.

What do I do for a double round robin with an odd number of teams?

Repeat the same rounds with home and away reversed. Each team then has two byes, one in each half, and meets every opponent twice.

Swiss system: pair the next round

    
For chess, darts, board-game and esports events where a full round robin takes too long. List the players best seed first (the Teams box above), type finished games below as Ana 1 - 0 Ben (equal numbers are a draw) or Cy bye, and get the next round's boards: players with the same score meet, nobody meets twice, the bye goes to someone who has not had one, and colours alternate. The table ranks by score, then Buchholz (the sum of your opponents' scores).

    
    
    
    
    

    

  


  

    
Americano: rotating partners for doubles nights

    
For social padel, pickleball, badminton and tennis nights where everyone plays with and against as many different people as possible. List the players in the Teams box above, say how many courts you have and how many rounds, and get a sheet of who partners whom each round. Games and sit-outs are shared evenly; repeat partners are avoided as far as the round count allows and counted below.

    
    
    
    
    
    
    

    

  


  

    
Mexicano: next round from the scores

    
The padel night format where each round is drawn from the table: the leaders play the leaders. List the players in the Teams box above, set the courts, and paste every finished game, one per line, like Ana & Ben 21-17 Cy & Dee. With no scores it draws round one at random. Each player gets their side's points, the best four play together (1 & 4 against 2 & 3, or a split that avoids a repeat partner), and whoever has played most sits out.

    
    
    
    
    
    
    

    

  


  

    
How it is built

    
Pairings: the circle method. One team stays fixed and the others rotate, so every pair meets exactly once per leg. With an odd number of teams an invisible extra team gives one real team a bye each round.

    
Home and away: set while the rounds are built. With an even number of teams the count of back-to-back home or away games is the minimum possible (teams minus two), and every team's home and away games differ by at most one. A double round robin repeats the rounds with every venue swapped.

    
Dates: rounds go on your chosen weekdays from the first date, jumping over skip dates. A team blackout takes only the clashing match out of its round and plays it in a makeup round after the season; if no round can be played on a date, that date is left unused and the page says so.

    
Courts and times: each match gets a slot by a seeded simulated-annealing search that evens out how often each team uses each court and each time. Reshuffle changes the seed.

    
Checked: a separate validator re-reads the finished schedule and confirms every pair meets the right number of times, no team plays twice in a round, home and away is balanced, no court is double-booked, and every date respects your weekdays, skip dates and blackouts. It cannot tell whether the schedule suits your league's own rules.

  


  

    
Common questions

    
How do I make a round-robin schedule for my league?

    
Type the team names one per line, pick the first date and the weekday you play on, and click Build the schedule. The generator uses the circle method, so every team plays every other team once (or twice for a double round robin), and shows each round with its date, court and time. Download it as a CSV, a calendar file or plain text to send to the league.

    
How does it handle an odd number of teams?

    
With an odd number of teams one team has a bye each round. The generator lists the bye so everybody can see which week they are off, and every team gets exactly one bye per leg of the season.

    
How are home and away games balanced?

    
Home and away is set while the rounds are built. With an even number of teams the number of back-to-back home or away games is the proven minimum, and every team's home and away games differ by at most one. With an odd number of teams nobody plays two home or two away games in a row. A double round robin is mirrored so each pair plays once at each home.

    
What if a team cannot play on a certain date?

    
Add the team and the date under blackout dates. Only the match that clashes is taken out of that round and played in a makeup round after the regular season; the rest of the round goes ahead. Skip dates, such as holidays, remove a date for everyone.

    
How are courts and time slots shared out?

    
If you list courts and time slots, the generator assigns each match to one so that every team gets a similar number of each court and each time. It uses a seeded search, so the same seed always gives the same schedule, and Reshuffle tries another one.

    
Can I build a play-off from the standings?

    
Yes. Type the results as lines like Hawks 3 - 2 Owls, choose how many teams qualify, and the page ranks the teams by points, goal difference and goals scored and builds a single-elimination bracket. If the field is not a power of two, the top seeds get a first-round bye.

    
Is my team list uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Everything is calculated in your browser from what you type, nothing is sent to a server, there are no accounts, and it works offline once the page has loaded.

A round is one set of games in which every team plays at most once, usually one night or one weekend. "Home/away breaks" counts the times a team has two home or two away games in a row across the whole single round robin; for an even league the minimum possible is the number of teams minus two, and the generator reaches it. A double round robin repeats the rounds with every venue reversed. If you have fewer courts than games per round, a round takes more than one night, so check the number of courts against the "games per round" column before you book.

Questions

How many weeks does a round robin take?

With an even number of teams, one fewer week than there are teams (8 teams: 7 weeks); with an odd number, as many weeks as teams (7 teams: 7 weeks), because one team has a bye each week. A double round robin takes twice as many. If you have fewer courts than matches per round, a round needs more than one night; the generator spreads courts and time slots for you.

How many games does each team play?

In a single round robin, every team plays every other team once, so n-1 games for n teams (a team with a bye plays one fewer than the number of rounds). In a double round robin, 2(n-1).

Is it better to have an even or an odd number of teams?

Even is simpler: nobody sits out. Odd leagues give every team exactly one bye in a single round robin and a perfect home and away pattern with no two home or two away games in a row. Neither is unfair; both are fully balanced.

For the method itself with a worked five-team example, read how to make a round-robin schedule, or copy the full fixtures from the round robin schedule template.

Questions

What is a round robin schedule template?

A fixture list for a set number of teams, labelled by team number, in which every team plays every other team once. Replace the numbers with your team names: Team 1 is the first name on your list, Team 2 the second, and so on. Home is listed first.

Why does the 8 team round robin have 7 rounds?

In each round every team plays once, and each team has 7 opponents, so 7 rounds. With 8 teams there are 4 games per round and 28 games in total.

What do I do with an odd number of teams?

One team sits out each round (a bye), so the schedule has as many rounds as teams. The 5, 7, 9 and 11 team tables below show the team with the bye in each round; every team gets exactly one.

Can I use these for a double round robin?

Yes. Play the same rounds again with home and away reversed. The generator does this for you with the double round robin option, and also puts real dates, courts and time slots on the rounds.
